questions.q: Power stations make electricity. Name the energy source of a nuclear power station.
questions.explain: A nuclear power station uses uranium as its fuel. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels.

questions.q: Power stations use different fuels. State the types of power station used in Singapore.
questions.explain: Singapore's power stations burn natural gas, with a few burning oil. Singapore has no coal-fired or nuclear power stations.

questions.q: Nuclear power stations make little pollution. Explain why Singapore does not use them.
choices: they need strong winds to work
questions.explain: A leak from a nuclear power station can harm people's health for many years. Singapore is small and crowded, so a leak would affect many people.

questions.q: Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels. State the energy stored in them.
questions.explain: Fossil fuels store chemical potential energy. It is released as heat when the fuel is burnt.

questions.q: Name the part of a power station where the fuel is burned.
questions.explain: The fuel is burnt in the furnace. The heat from the furnace then boils water in the boiler.

questions.q: Fuel burns in a power station furnace. State the energy it gives out.
questions.explain: Burning fuel releases its chemical potential energy as heat energy. This heat is used to boil water into steam.

questions.q: Moving steam pushes and spins a set of blades. Name this power station part.
questions.explain: The turbine has blades that are pushed round by moving steam. It changes the energy of the steam into kinetic energy.

questions.q: Name the power station part that changes kinetic energy into electrical energy.
questions.explain: The generator is turned by the turbine. It changes this kinetic energy into electrical energy.

questions.q: Identify the order of parts in a fossil fuel power station.
questions.explain: The fuel burns in the furnace, the heat boils water in the boiler, the steam spins the turbine, and the turbine turns the generator.

questions.q: In a power station, steam turns the turbine. Name the part that makes the steam.
questions.explain: The boiler uses heat from the furnace to boil water. The steam it makes then turns the turbine.

questions.q: Electricity reaches homes through a grid. Describe an electricity grid.
questions.explain: An electricity grid is a network of cables and substations. It carries electricity from power stations to homes and other buildings.

questions.q: Electricity leaves a power station. Name the device it passes through first.
questions.explain: As electricity leaves the power station, a step-up transformer raises its voltage. It is then sent along the long cables of the grid.

questions.q: Electricity goes from power stations to homes. State where its voltage is stepped down.
questions.explain: The voltage is stepped down at substations near homes. This makes it safe for use in homes.

questions.q: Electricity from the grid reaches a home. Name the last device it passed through.
questions.explain: Just before electricity reaches homes, a step-down transformer lowers its voltage. So it is the last device it passes through.

questions.q: Identify the path of electricity from a power station to homes.
questions.explain: A step-up transformer raises the voltage at the power station, the cables carry it across the country, and a step-down transformer lowers it near homes.

questions.q: Electricity is sent through long cables at high voltage. Explain why.
choices: to allow the use of transformers
questions.explain: At high voltage the current in the cables is small. A smaller current heats the cables less, so less energy is lost on the way.

questions.q: The voltage in long cables is stepped up. Predict the change in current.
questions.explain: When a transformer steps up the voltage, the current is stepped down. So the current in the long cables decreases.

questions.q: Describe the structure of a simple transformer.
choices: two coils on an iron core
two coils on a plastic core
one coil on an iron core
two iron cores in one coil
questions.explain: A simple transformer has two coils of wire wound on an iron core. The iron core links the two coils.

questions.q: A transformer has two coils. Name the coil connected to the input voltage.
questions.explain: The coil connected to the input voltage is the primary coil. The coil that gives the output voltage is the secondary coil.

questions.q: Transformers change voltage. Name the type of current that transformers work with.
questions.explain: Transformers only work with alternating current (a.c.). Batteries give direct current (d.c.), which a transformer cannot change.

questions.q: A device changes 25 kV to 400 kV. Identify the device.
questions.explain: The device raises the voltage from 25 kV to 400 kV. A device that raises voltage is a step-up transformer.

questions.q: A laptop adapter plugs into the mains socket. Identify what the adapter acts as.
questions.explain: A laptop adapter lowers the mains voltage to the small voltage the laptop needs. So it acts as a step-down transformer.

questions.q: A laptop needs an adapter for the mains. Explain why it cannot plug in directly.
questions.explain: The mains voltage is about 230 V, which is far more than a laptop needs. Plugging it in directly would damage the laptop.

questions.q: Step-up transformers raise the voltage. Identify where step-up transformers are used.
questions.explain: Step-up transformers are used at power stations. They raise the voltage before the electricity is sent along the long cables.

questions.q: Batteries are used in torches and phones. Explain why batteries are important.
questions.explain: Batteries are small and light and can be carried around. They let us use electricity where there is no mains supply.

questions.q: A battery converts chemical potential energy. State the energy it is converted into.
questions.explain: A battery converts its stored chemical potential energy into electrical energy.

questions.q: State an advantage of a rechargeable battery.
questions.explain: A rechargeable battery can be charged and used again many times. This saves money and makes less waste.
